# FAMIS Eligibility Requirements

## Uninsured/Coverage Requirement

"Any child covered under a group health plan or under health insurance coverage, as defined in § 2791 of the Public Health Services Act (42 USC § 300gg-91(a) and (b)(1)), shall not be eligible for FAMIS."

Additionally: "Only uninsured children shall be eligible for FAMIS."

## Income Limit

"Children from birth to age 19 years who have income above the Medicaid-eligible limit at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, with a 5% income disregard, shall be income eligible to participate in FAMIS."

## Key Point

The regulation specifies that applicants cannot have creditable health insurance coverage, which is defined as coverage meeting the standards in 42 CFR 457.10. Medicare, Medicaid, and FAMIS itself are explicitly excluded from this restriction.

# 12VAC30-141-100. General conditions of eligibility.

**Section Title and Full Text:**

"A. An LDSS, DMAS, or the CPU determines eligibility for Title XXI services." The regulation establishes that eligibility determinations involve local departments of social services, the Department of Medical Assistance Services, or the Central Processing Unit.

The section requires that "FAMIS shall be in effect statewide" and specifies the program serves children consistent with federal requirements found at 42 CFR sections 457.310, 457.315, and 457.320.

**Key Eligibility Requirements:**

Individuals must be "Financially eligible to receive services as established using the methods and standards described in subsection F" and meet nonfinancial conditions. These conditions include being under 19 years old, Commonwealth residents, and uninsured. The regulation defines "Creditable health insurance coverage" as coverage meeting 42 CFR 457.10 standards.

Citizenship requirements permit "United States citizens; United States nationals; Qualified noncitizens" and those "lawfully residing in the United States." The section outlines specific immigration statuses and provides detailed provisions for pending asylum applications and other protected statuses.

Financial eligibility uses modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) methodologies, with children eligible at incomes up to "200% of the federal poverty level, with a 5% income disregard."

**Historical Notes:**

Derived from Virginia Register Volume 19, Issue 21 (effective August 1, 2003); amended through Volume 35, Issue 20 (effective June 26, 2019).

# 42 CFR § 457.310 - Targeted Low-Income Child

**Section (a) - Definition:**
"A targeted low-income child is a child who meets the standards set forth below and the eligibility standards established by the State under § 457.320."

**Section (b) - Standards Introduction:**
"A targeted low-income child must meet the following standards:"

**Section (b)(2) - No Other Coverage Standard:**
"A targeted low-income child must not be—

(i) Found eligible or potentially eligible for Medicaid under policies of the State plan (determined through either the Medicaid application process or the screening process described at § 457.350), except for eligibility under § 435.214 of this chapter (related to coverage for family planning services);

(ii) Covered under a group health plan or under health insurance coverage, as defined in section 2791 of the Public Health Service Act, unless the plan or health insurance coverage program has been in operation since before July 1, 1997 and is administered by a State that receives no Federal funds for the program's operation. A child is not considered covered under a group health plan or health insurance coverage if the child does not have reasonable geographic access to care under that plan."

**Amendment Dates:** [66 FR 2675, Jan. 11, 2001, as amended at 71 FR 39229, July 12, 2006; 77 FR 17214, Mar. 23, 2012; 81 FR 86463, Nov. 30, 2016]

# 42 U.S. Code § 1397jj - Definition of "Targeted Low-Income Child"

## Subsection (b)(1)

According to the statute, a "targeted low-income child" means a child who meets three criteria:

**(b)(1)(A):** "who has been determined eligible by the State for child health assistance under the State plan"

**(b)(1)(B):** The child must be either a low-income child OR satisfy specific income thresholds relative to the medicaid applicable income level

**(b)(1)(C):** The child cannot be eligible for Medicaid or "covered under a group health plan or under health insurance coverage (as such terms are defined in section 300gg–91 of this title)"

The third requirement establishes that CHIP covers children who lack other insurance options, distinguishing CHIP from Medicaid and employer-based plans.

## Basic Eligibility Requirements

To qualify for FAMIS, children must live in Virginia, be uninsured, be under age 19, be United States citizens or lawfully residing immigrants, and live in families that meet income rules.

Only uninsured children shall be eligible for FAMIS. A child is not considered to be insured if the health insurance plan covering the child does not have a network of providers in the area where the child resides.

Income standards for FAMIS are based on a comparison of countable income to 200% of the federal poverty level for the family size. FAMIS covers services including dental care, doctor visits, emergency care, hospital visits, mental health care, prescription medicine, tests and X-rays, vaccinations, vision care, and well-child check-ups.

## Administration

FAMIS is a comprehensive health coverage program for Virginia's children. The program is administered by the Department of Medical Assistance Services (DMAS) and funded by the state and federal governments.
